tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics > A. N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptors, 1st, 3rd and 4th paragraphs; Table 3, NMDAR rows
tasks.extracted: The review reports ketamine as a non-competitive open-channel blocker at the phencyclidine site inside the NMDA receptor channel, with a trapping capability of about 86%, against more than 98% for phencyclidine and 100% for MK-801. Reported affinities for racemic ketamine in the presence of magnesium span Ki 0.18 to 3.1 micromolar across about twenty studies, including human cortex values of 0.42 (SE 0.03) and 0.67 (SE 0.15) micromolar; which subunits are blocked most depends on the magnesium present, and one cited study found no subunit difference. The tabulated values come mostly from rodent tissue, recombinant receptors in cell lines and oocytes, with a few human post-mortem brain samples.

tasks.locator: II. Pharmacokinetics > A. Metabolism, 1st to 3rd paragraphs; Figure 1 and Figure 2 legends
tasks.extracted: Ketamine is first N-demethylated to norketamine, mainly by the liver enzymes CYP2B6 and CYP3A4, and the reaction is stereoselective; norketamine is then hydroxylated, chiefly by CYP2A6 and CYP2B6, to the hydroxynorketamines, or converted to dehydronorketamine, with minor routes giving hydroxyketamines and hydroxyphenyl metabolites. The review attributes part of the variation between people to differences in how much of these enzymes they have.

tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics > A. N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptors, 5th and 6th paragraphs; Table 3, norKET, DHNK and HNK rows
tasks.extracted: Norketamine also blocks the NMDA receptor, with S-norketamine reported at Ki 1.70 to 2.25 micromolar and the R form about eight times weaker (13.0 to 26.46 micromolar). Dehydronorketamine and the hydroxynorketamines are weak or inactive there: (2S,6S)-hydroxynorketamine displaces the reference ligand only at about 10.4 to 21.0 micromolar and (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine not appreciably (above 100 micromolar), and neither inhibits NMDA-evoked currents at concentrations up to 10 micromolar. At 50 micromolar, which the review calls higher than antidepressant-relevant, (2R,6R)-hydroxynorketamine inhibited those currents by about 40% against more than 90% for ketamine in the same experiment.

tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics, introductory paragraph; sections B to I; Table 3
tasks.extracted: The review's working test is whether a target is affected within the concentrations reached in people, which by its own Table 1 are about 0.8 micromolar after the antidepressant infusion and about 5 to 10 micromolar at anaesthesia. Most other targets fall outside that range, at about 10 to 1000 micromolar: opioid receptors in the tens to hundreds, sigma receptors 19 to 139, the serotonin, noradrenaline and dopamine transporters mostly above 60, sodium and calcium channels in the hundreds to thousands, and GABA-A effects only at hundreds, with no binding seen at subanaesthetic doses in a human imaging study. The exceptions the review names are nicotinic receptors (alpha4beta4 blocked at IC50 0.24 micromolar in oocytes, alpha3beta4 at 3.1, alpha7 at about 17 to 20), HCN1 channels (8.2 to 15.6 micromolar) and a muscarinic value reported both at 45 and at 5.7 micromolar in different systems. The review states that many of these findings have not been confirmed by independent laboratories.

tasks.locator: II. Pharmacokinetics > C. Distribution, 1st paragraph; II. Pharmacokinetics > D. Elimination, last paragraph
tasks.extracted: Ketamine distributes rapidly into well-perfused tissue including the brain, with plasma protein binding between 10% and 50% and a steady-state volume of distribution of 3 to 5 l/kg. The review states that the brain levels of ketamine and its metabolites in people are not known, so human brain exposure is inferred only from rodent data.

tasks.locator: IV. Conclusions > A. (R)- and (S)-Ketamine as Antidepressants, 1st and 3rd paragraphs; > B. Utility of Ketamine's Hydroxynorketamine Metabolites as Drug Treatments, 1st paragraph; Footnotes (competing interests)
tasks.extracted: The metabolite account is preclinical as the review presents it: hydroxynorketamines are reported to produce antidepressant-like behaviour in rodents without the sensory dissociation, ataxia or self-administration seen with ketamine, and R-ketamine is reported to be a more potent and longer-lasting antidepressant than S-ketamine across rodent tests. The review states that no clinical study of R-ketamine in patients with depression had been published and that no clinical study had compared the two forms with each other or with the racemate, and it cites no human study in which a hydroxynorketamine was given. Most of the authors are named as co-inventors on patents or patent applications covering those metabolites, and much of the supporting work comes from their own laboratories, including data marked unpublished.

tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics > E. Monoaminergic Receptors and Transporters, 2nd to 4th paragraphs
tasks.extracted: On dopamine the review reports both sides: ketamine was described as a high-affinity D2 partial agonist (Ki 0.055 to 1.0 micromolar) and three human imaging studies reported reduced striatal D2 binding after subanaesthetic dosing, while two other human imaging studies found no change in striatal D2 availability, a human study found that a D2 blocker did not stop ketamine's psychosis-like effects, and a mouse study found no functional activity at any dopamine receptor subtype up to 10 micromolar and no change in evoked dopamine release.

tasks.locator: III. Pharmacodynamics > A. N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptors, 5th paragraph against Table 3; II. Pharmacokinetics > D. Elimination, 2nd paragraph
tasks.extracted: Reporting problems the first reader found and this claim respects: affinity ranges printed in the text omit values listed in the review's own Table 3 and mix Ki with IC50 values within one range, in each case in the direction that strengthens the contrast drawn, so metabolite affinities should be traced to the primary papers; and a unit conversion for norketamine in children's urine is wrong by more than two orders of magnitude. The review's general statements about safety, for which it reviews no evidence, are not used here.

tasks.extracted: 36 within-person placebo-controlled studies in 725 healthy adults were pooled (22 using the BPRS, 14 the PANSS), all giving ketamine into a vein. Of the 36, 27 were double-blind, 5 single-blind, 3 unblinded and 1 did not report it; order was randomized in 30 and not in 6; the time from the start of the infusion to the rating was reported for 17 studies (1 to 120 minutes) and not for 19. Only 5 studies excluded people with previous ketamine exposure, and the authors state that ketamine's effects make blinding very difficult. The reported sex split (533 men) cannot be reproduced from the Table, which leaves the sex of 107 people unstated.
